arguments.reasoning: Identify the parent process that spawned rm.
Check whether parent is update-notifier / apt maintenance script.

steps.text: This looks like the standard Ubuntu update-motd hwe-eol script that creates and removes a temp file in /var/lib/update-notifier—benign behavior. I have enough evidence now, so I'll just submit with the entities, maybe citing the deleted_file relation.

submission.reasoning: I checked the alert: root ran /bin/rm (pid 5109) with 'rm -f /var/lib/update-notifier/tmp.aHJK3eQBrz'. Its parent is /bin/dash running '/bin/sh /etc/update-motd.d/95-hwe-eol'. That is Ubuntu's standard MOTD script. It checks whether the hardware enablement (HWE) kernel stack has reached end of life. It makes a temporary file under /var/lib/update-notifier and deletes it when done. Only that one temp file in the update-notifier directory was removed. Nothing was shredded and no critical directory was touched. This is routine system maintenance, not data destruction.
